solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Start of exciting film, a blockbuster

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from exciting

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: A thrilling opening to a movie that turns out to be a box-office hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand, lavish film on a huge scale is a typical box-office blockbuster.

clue.text: An old work about an Indian city

indicators.note: about signals turning the assembled pieces round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
op (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: An ancient piece of writing describing a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the whole string ANOOP. Poona is the older spelling of Pune, in western India.
explanation.definitionFit: Poona, now usually called Pune, is a large city in Maharashtra, India.

clue.text: Trick woman into breaking up a group of stars

parts.note: to con someone is to trick them
Stella is a woman's name

indicators.note: breaking up the word into scatters its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cons a woman into ending her relationship with a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A named pattern of stars in the night sky, such as Orion, is a constellation.

clue.text: Flourish container for grain husks?

parts.note: bran is the husks separated from cereal grain
a dish is a container for food

explanation.surface: A question asking whether an ornate gesture is really a bowl for cereal husks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical reading of the answer as two words: a dish for bran.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword or stick is to wave it about showily, a synonym.

clue.text: Vocally expresses disapproval of alcoholic drink

indicators.note: vocally says the phrase that follows is to be heard spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a crowd that boos is expressing disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone loudly objects to alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal slang for strong drink such as beer or spirits.

clue.text: A row involving Irish transport organisation

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: taken as written
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A quarrel involving an Irish transport company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a line, not a quarrel as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A company running scheduled passenger flights is an organisation providing transport.

clue.text: Loss of girl's looks and bearing

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so girl's gives DI'S
one's appearance is one's looks and general bearing

explanation.surface: A young woman is losing her good looks and poise.
explanation.definitionFit: When something goes missing it has vanished, so its vanishing is a loss.

clue.text: Liquid food caught on? Just a touch

parts.note: soup is liquid food
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether soup has caught on, answered with: only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupcon is a tiny trace or hint, borrowed from French for suspicion.

clue.text: Rainstorm in Ulster county, on the rocks some say?

parts.note: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland (Ulster)

indicators.note: some say means this part is heard rather than seen, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a business on the rocks is broke, or poor

explanation.surface: A deluge in Northern Ireland, with someone mentioning drinks served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' suggests a drink with ice; here it means in financial trouble, i.e. poor. County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy, sudden fall of rain is a rainstorm.

clue.text: Self-satisfied, having rejected sweets

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: gums are chewy sweets, as in fruit gums

explanation.surface: Someone smugly turns down the sweets on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A complacent person pleased with themselves is self-satisfied.

clue.text: Class going round rear of medieval fortress

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a caste is a social class

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter, here from medieval

explanation.surface: A school class on a trip around a medieval fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified medieval stronghold is a castle.

clue.text: Reduced charge for salad ingredient

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: cost is the charge for something

explanation.surface: A discounted price for something in a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of lettuce, a common salad ingredient.

clue.text: Impression made by one politician introducing bill

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is Member of Parliament
a bill passed into law becomes an act

explanation.surface: A single MP makes their mark by bringing in a new bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the effect or strong impression something makes.

clue.text: Give the game away? A clumsy greengrocer might

definitions.meaning: to reveal a secret, an idiom
literally, a careless vegetable seller might drop legumes everywhere

explanation.surface: A clumsy grocer reveals a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to disclose a secret; literally it means scattering legumes.

clue.text: Specious excuse from platoon leader regarding message

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of platoon

parts.note: re means regarding, as in a letter
a text is a message sent by phone

explanation.surface: An army officer offers a feeble excuse about a message.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to cover the real one.

clue.text: Communications satellite rattles frightfully

indicators.note: frightfully suggests the letters are badly shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A satellite makes alarming rattling noises.
explanation.walkthrough: Telstar, launched in 1962, was the first satellite to relay live television across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was a pioneering satellite for relaying TV and phone signals.

clue.text: Personification of sun initially shining over Llandudno

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: The sun personified beaming down over a Welsh seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Llandudno is a seaside resort in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol was the Roman god of the sun, the sun in personal form.

clue.text: Particular sci-fi film seized by Irish legislators

indicators.note: seized by means held inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament
E.T. is Spielberg's science-fiction film

explanation.surface: A science-fiction movie is confiscated by Irish lawmakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a single item or point, a particular in noun use.

clue.text: Extremely coarse, genuine breakfast food?

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters of coarse

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: A very rough but authentic morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflakes and porridge are kinds of grain food eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Shrewd girl in outskirts of Coventry

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
outskirts are the edges, the first and last letters of Coventry

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A clever young woman living on the edge of Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny is a word for astute and careful, especially with money.

clue.text: In maturity, engineers see eye to eye

indicators.note: in places the engineers inside the word for maturity

parts.note: age means maturity
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: As they grow older, engineers come to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye is an idiom for sharing the same view.

clue.text: House in Home Counties beside busy road

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the South East, SE
the M1 motorway, read as MI, is a busy road

explanation.surface: A home in the commuter belt beside a busy road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London. A semi is a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached home, one of a pair sharing a wall.

clue.text: Leaseholders finally circumvent any rent mix-up

indicators.note: finally means take the final letter of circumvent
a mix-up shuffles these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Tenants try to dodge a muddle over rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenantry is a collective word for the tenants on an estate.

clue.text: Way fashionable eighteenth century elegist identifies fish

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
in means fashionable
Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard (1751)

explanation.surface: A trendy old poet names a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray with a venomous barbed tail is a type of fish.

clue.text: Large jug sheep found by river

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A big jug discovered by sheep near a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a wide-mouthed pitcher for water.
